initial_requirements: UK fishing vessel masters and owners need an onboard electronic logbook that replaces paper recording for regulated fishing activity. The system should capture required logbook, transhipment, and landing information and transmit compliant reports to the appropriate fisheries administration. It should help vessel operators review and submit accurate records while accommodating relevant data supplied by other onboard systems.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What are the primary outcomes you want this onboard electronic logbook to achieve for vessel masters and owners—for example, which recording, review, and submission capabilities are most important, and what specific tasks should it replace or simplify compared with the current paper process?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
The main outcome is to let the crew record all the required fishing activity onboard accurately and in one place, without relying on paper logbooks. It should make it easy for the master or owner to review entries, correct mistakes before submission, and send the required reports electronically to the right fisheries authority.
It should replace the manual paper recording, the separate re-copying of information for transhipments and landings, and a lot of the end-of-trip admin that currently takes time and can introduce errors. Ideally it also reduces double entry by pulling in data from other onboard systems where that’s available, so the operator isn’t typing the same information more than once.

turns.interviewer_utterance: At what point in the voyage or reporting cycle should the logbook data be submitted electronically—for example, after each catch event, before arrival in port, at landing/transhipment, or only after the master or owner has completed a final review—and are there any deadlines or triggers that govern submission timing?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
My understanding is that the system needs to support ongoing recording during the voyage, but submission timing will depend on the type of report and the regulatory trigger. In practice, some entries may need to be sent at landing or transhipment, while the full logbook may be finalised after the master has reviewed it and then submitted within whatever deadline the fisheries administration requires.
I don’t know the exact deadlines offhand, and I’d want to check the rules for each administration because those timings can differ. What matters most operationally is that the system clearly prompts the user when a submission is due and doesn’t let them miss a required reporting point.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Since reporting timings and requirements can differ by fisheries administration, what specific rules should the system support for each administration—for example, which report types are required, what deadlines or trigger events apply, and how should the system behave when a vessel operates under more than one administration's rules?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
We’d need the system to handle the rules set by each relevant administration separately, because the report types and timing can vary depending on where the vessel is operating and who the report is going to. I’m not certain of every specific rule set today, but at a minimum it should know which administration applies for the trip and then apply the right required report types, deadlines, and triggers for that case.
If a vessel is operating under more than one administration’s rules, the system should probably avoid mixing them and instead make it clear which requirements are active for that voyage or report. If the rules conflict, I’d expect it to flag that for the operator rather than guessing, but I’d need to verify the exact policy with the regulatory team.

turns.interviewer_utterance: When data from other onboard systems is unavailable, what should the logbook let users do manually instead, and are there any rules or safeguards for those manual entries before they can be submitted?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
If other onboard data isn’t available, the logbook should let the user enter the same core details manually so they can still complete the required record and keep fishing operations moving. That would include the voyage and catch-related information the report needs, rather than forcing them to stop because an automated feed failed.
Before submission, I’d expect the system to do some basic checks for missing or inconsistent values and clearly show anything that still needs attention. It should probably distinguish manual entries from imported ones for audit purposes, but I’d need to confirm whether there are any formal validation or sign-off rules beyond the normal review by the master.

turns.interviewer_utterance: How should the logbook behave when the vessel has no network connectivity or cannot reach the fisheries authority at the time a report is due—for example, should it continue capturing data offline, queue submissions for later, and if so what expectations are there for retries, notifications, or user actions once connectivity returns?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
It should definitely keep capturing data offline, because these vessels won’t always have a reliable connection. If a report is due and the system can’t reach the authority, I’d expect it to queue the submission and keep trying automatically once connectivity comes back.
The user should be clearly told that a report is pending and whether anything still needs checking before it can go out. Once connection returns, the system should either submit automatically or prompt the master to confirm if there’s any risk of duplicate or partial sending, but the exact retry timing and notification rules would need to be agreed with the authorities.

slots.name: project_goals
slots.value: Enable crew to record all required fishing activity onboard accurately in one place without paper logbooks, allow the master or owner to review and correct entries before submission, electronically send required reports to the correct fisheries authority, replace manual paper recording and separate re-copying for transhipments and landings, reduce end-of-trip administration and errors, and minimize double entry by reusing data from other onboard systems where available.

slots.name: stakeholder_roles
slots.value: Crew record activity onboard; master or owner reviews entries, corrects mistakes, and submits reports; fisheries authority receives the electronic reports.

slots.name: functional_needs
slots.value: Capture required fishing activity in a single onboard electronic logbook, support review and correction of entries before submission, generate and transmit compliant electronic reports for logbook, transhipment, and landing information, import/reuse data from other onboard systems to reduce double entry, prompt users when submissions are due, and allow manual entry of core voyage and catch details when onboard system data is unavailable.

slots.name: business_rules
slots.value: Records must meet required logbook, transhipment, and landing reporting obligations, apply the relevant fisheries administration's rules for the voyage, and be submitted to the correct fisheries administration.

slots.name: data_entities
slots.value: Fishing activity log entries, transhipment information, landing information, compliant reports, data imported from other onboard systems, manual core voyage and catch details, and administration-specific reporting requirements.

slots.name: constraints
slots.value: Intended for UK fishing vessel masters and owners; must replace paper recording and support electronic submission to the relevant fisheries authority.

slots.name: quality_concerns
slots.value: Accuracy of recorded information, reduction of errors and double entry, ease of review and correction, compliance of submitted reports, and basic validation of missing or inconsistent values before submission.

slots.name: boundary_conditions
slots.value: When data from other onboard systems is unavailable, users may need to enter information manually; the system must still support required recording and submission without relying on imported data. If more than one administration's rules apply or rules conflict, the system should clearly show which requirements are active and flag conflicts rather than guessing.

slots.name: submission_timing
slots.value: The system must support ongoing recording during the voyage, with submission timing varying by report type and regulatory trigger; some reports may be due at landing or transhipment, while the full logbook may be finalised after master review and submitted within the relevant fisheries administration deadline, with prompts to alert users when submission is due.

slots.name: offline_operation
slots.value: The system should continue capturing data offline when connectivity is unavailable, queue pending submissions, retry automatically when connection returns, and alert the user that a report is pending; it may either submit automatically or prompt the master to confirm if there is any risk of duplicate or partial sending.

slots.name: data_source_integrations
slots.value: The system should pull in data from other onboard systems when available to reduce double entry and avoid retyping the same information.

slots.name: correction_workflow
slots.value: The master or owner should be able to review recorded entries and correct mistakes before submission.

slots.name: audit_trail_requirements
slots.value: Manual entries should be distinguishable from imported entries for audit purposes; no formal validation or sign-off rules have been confirmed beyond normal master review.

slots.name: administration_specific_reporting_rules
slots.value: The system must support the rules of each relevant fisheries administration separately, including the applicable report types, deadlines, and trigger events for the voyage, and make it clear which administration's requirements are active. If rules conflict, it should flag the issue for the operator.

slots.name: submission_deadline_notifications
slots.value: The system should clearly prompt the user when a submission is due and help prevent missed reporting points.

slots.name: regulatory_trigger_configuration
slots.value: The system should apply the required report types, deadlines, and trigger events based on the applicable fisheries administration for the trip.

slots.name: multi_administration_support
slots.value: If a vessel is operating under more than one administration's rules, the system should avoid mixing requirements, clearly indicate which rules are active for the voyage or report, and flag conflicts for operator review.

slots.name: manual_fallback_when_integrations_unavailable
slots.value: If onboard data feeds are unavailable, the system should let users manually enter the same core voyage and catch details needed for the report so operations can continue.

slots.name: offline_data_capture_and_sync
slots.value: The system should support offline capture and later synchronization when connectivity returns, including queued submissions and automatic retries.

slots.name: jurisdiction_selection_for_voyage
slots.value: The system should know which fisheries administration applies for the trip and use that jurisdiction to determine the active reporting requirements.

slots.name: conflict_resolution_workflow
slots.value: If rules conflict between administrations, the system should flag the conflict and show which requirements are active for the voyage or report rather than guessing.

slots.name: connectivity_assumptions
slots.value: Vessels cannot rely on a stable network connection; the system must work when connectivity is intermittent or unavailable.

slots.name: offline_capture_requirements
slots.value: The system should keep capturing data when offline, preserve pending reports for later submission, and indicate to the user that items are awaiting transmission.

slots.name: store_and_forward_submission_queue
slots.value: If submission cannot be sent immediately, the system should queue the report and forward it automatically when connectivity is restored, with user visibility of pending items.

slots.name: sync_conflict_handling
slots.value: When queued or partially sent submissions are synchronized later, the system should guard against duplicate or partial sending and surface any need for master confirmation.

abduction_history.surprising_fact: Submission deadlines and reporting triggers differ by fisheries administration, and the user does not know the exact timings but wants the system to prompt reliably so required reporting points are not missed.
abduction_history.suspected_reason: The logbook may need to support multiple regulatory regimes and configurable deadline rules because vessels can operate across administrations or under changing compliance obligations, so the product likely needs a rules-driven notification and scheduling mechanism rather than hard-coded submission timing.

abduction_history.surprising_fact: The vessel may need to continue recording onboard activity even when data from other onboard systems is unavailable, while also handling submissions under multiple potentially conflicting administration rules without guessing.
abduction_history.suspected_reason: This suggests the logbook must be resilient to poor connectivity and partial onboard data availability, and it likely needs strong compliance safeguards because fishing voyages can cross regulatory boundaries or be governed by changing jurisdictional rules. The product therefore may require offline-first operation, clear fallback to manual entry, and explicit auditability of which rule set was applied and when.

abduction_history.surprising_fact: The stakeholder expects the system to support ongoing onboard recording and submission prompts, but the current requirements still do not state how it should behave when the vessel has no network connectivity or cannot reach the fisheries authority at the time a submission is due.
abduction_history.suspected_reason: This likely indicates an operational need for an offline-first logbook that can continue capturing records and queue submissions until connectivity returns, because fishing vessels may operate in areas with intermittent or no communications and compliance cannot depend on live connectivity.

abduction_history.surprising_fact: The stakeholder wants the system to either submit automatically or prompt the master to confirm when connectivity returns, because there may be a risk of duplicate or partial sending after offline queuing.
abduction_history.suspected_reason: This suggests the reporting workflow must protect against duplicate transmissions and incomplete payloads in an intermittent-connectivity environment. The product likely needs explicit acknowledgement, idempotency, and transmission-status handling so the vessel can safely retry or resume submissions without creating compliance issues or duplicate records at the fisheries authority.
